data.body:
Second remediation round (2026-08-21), against the findings of the prior plan review. Every claim in the description was re-verified against the tree at origin/main; three were wrong and are corrected.

1. BLOCKING (prior review): the AC-3 guard could not pass. The plan asserted "exactly one definition of the synthetic-timeout construct under src/rebar, owner git_outcome.py exempt". Verified false: the synthetic rc-124 `git timed out after` result is ALSO built at src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:604 inside run_git_write._bounded_once — which is precisely the shared runner the shims are supposed to fold INTO — and at seven further sites outside _store (_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:212, _snapshot/git_fetch.py:137, _commands/fsck_repair.py:121, _commands/fsck_tracker_health.py:197, _commands/_init_probe.py:72, opcert_service/workspace.py:84, review_bot/gerrit_client.py:486), each with its own semantics and none in Scope. So the guard is now split in two, with two different owners, because these are two different constructs: git_outcome.py owns the marker STRINGS (Guard A), gitutil.py owns the synthetic-timeout CONSTRUCTION (Guard B), and Guard B is scoped to src/rebar/_store.

2. BLOCKING (prior review): the symbol at event_commit_git.py:64 is `_run_git`, not `_git`. Corrected; push.py:71 and sync.py:66 are indeed `_git`.

3. NEW, found this round: `_advisory_lock._is_cas_mismatch` is at line 285, not 272. Corrected.

4. Guard A cannot be a text grep. The four marker atoms appear in ordinary comments and docstrings across src/rebar (_mcp_reads.py:405, _lib_reads.py:313, _snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:20,398, _cli/_llm_commands.py:86, _commands/fsck_tracker_health.py:179, and a dozen explanatory comments inside gitutil.py and push_classify.py themselves). A grep guard would fail on prose forever. Guard A therefore parses each file and inspects only non-docstring `ast.Constant` string literals. Prototyped against the current tree: 14 literal hits across all of src/rebar, of which only 5 are inside the two Scope directories, and after the refactor exactly two remain — gitutil._LOCK_REF_RE (parses the ref name out of the exhaustion message) and _reclaim_if_stale_index_lock's os.path.join of the lock file PATH. Both are named in the description as expected escapes with reasons, since neither is a verdict.

5. Guard B is a conjunction, not a token: an `ast.Call` to subprocess.CompletedProcess carrying BOTH the int literal 124 AND a str/f-string argument containing "timed out after". A bare `grep -rn "timed out after"` was the prior review's other objection and would still match push_classify.py:126, where "git timed out after" is a legitimate TRANSPORT marker row that must survive.

6. ADVISORY (prior review): AC-6 was a near-duplicate of AC-2, reusing AC-2's own injection test as its evidence. Removed; push_recovery.py stays in Scope and its retry requirement is folded into AC-2. Remaining bundled-`and` criteria were split so each is independently verifiable.

7. Narrative claim trimmed: "the synthetic result is treated as retriable by only one" is retained, but the bug reference `unheedful-custodial-bluebottle` was dropped from the Context for space; the `wrongful-chemic-squeaker` claim was verified — s3_doctor.py:27 imports gitutil.run_git_write/is_transient_object_read_error, while sync._union_merge (sync.py:174) and push_recovery._merge_with_transport_retry (push_recovery.py:263) go through the unretried `_git` / `core._git` seam and retry TRANSPORT only.

Also verified as TRUE and left unchanged: gitutil.py:215/221/517, push_classify.py:48/61/110, _ref_lock_push.py:68/74, event_append.py:465, and that the named pinning test files all exist (the reconciler ones live under tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/, which the Testing section now says explicitly).
